title: Choose Metacrok's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Spec Label. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Spec Label
options.lineage: D2C product labels and ingredient panels (Minimalist, Aesop, nutrition-facts typography)
options.thesis: Every competitor is read like a product label: its angle mix printed as an ingredient list, its audience as 'made for'.
options.viewport: Results open on a row of tall label cards, one per brand in its own saturated SKU colour, each listing 'Ingredients: pain point 35%, offer 18%…' in huge type, with your brand's label set beside them and the 'missing ingredient' (whitespace) circled in yellow.
options.risk: Can tip into a beauty-only look; the label grammar must stay generic enough for snacks or apparel founders.

raised.raise: A corrected read or edited audience stays lit in one change colour until you regenerate.
Yellow means one thing only: open space nobody owns.
What we observed is drawn solid; what the AI inferred (audiences, positions) is drawn dashed.
The ad wall: the ad you focus grows to show its read while the rest dim.
Length is the number: every bar and every days-running mark is drawn exactly to scale.

options.label: The Year-in-Review Story
options.thesis: Your niche told as a sequence of full-bleed colour fields, one finding per field in enormous type.
options.viewport: A magenta field filling the screen: 'Your rivals said “glow” 41 times.' with the next finding peeking from the right.
options.risk: The most familiar direction; founders have seen this format every December, and dense comparison is harder to read in it.

options.label: Typographic Tiles
options.lineage: metro-style flat tiles with giant lowercase type
options.thesis: Each finding is a flat colour tile; type cropped off the edge is the interface.
options.viewport: A sideways panorama: 'whitespace' cropped in giant lowercase across a lime tile, competitor tiles flipping to fresh stats.
options.case: Fuses cleanly (findings as tiles, colour as content) and stays clear, but Indian D2C founders have no attachment to the tile world.
options.risk: Reads as a 2012 phone UI when the type is not huge.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.thesis: Competitors as flights reranked by how long their ads have run.
options.viewport: A departures board of ads ranked by days running.
options.case: Founders don't read their niche as a timetable; loses audience and clarity.
options.kept: Changes hold their highlight until acknowledged.
options.risk: A metaphor with no link to marketing.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each decision point signs only the choices ahead.
options.viewport: One yellow band: 'Whitespace → founder story, 12 ads away'.
options.case: Too single-colour for a brief that asks for more colour.
options.kept: One colour reserved for one meaning.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: State carried by line form on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: Ads as needle lines on one rail.
options.case: Beautiful but cold and colour-starved; founders can't read it at a glance.
options.kept: Observed vs inferred shown by line form.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Ads as poster rows; the focused one expands.
options.viewport: Rows of competitor ads by angle.
options.case: Good for browsing ads, weak for comparison and maps.
options.kept: Focus expands one ad, dims the rest.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Shape and length encode exact quantity.
options.viewport: A vertical staff of ad durations.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS analytics dashboard, like Foreplay or Motion, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, KPI row, charts grid, ad gallery.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every ad-spy tool by design.
